title: Introducing LiteLLM Customer Management | liteLLM
summary: Track customer spend and set organization, team, and member budgets with LiteLLM AI Gateway. Use the APIs to build these controls into your product.
body_markdown:
Illustrative customer traffic flows through LiteLLM into Customer Management. Organization, team, and member budgets use three views of the same request cost.


Published: Nov 13, 2026


[Ishaan Jaffer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/reffajnaahsi/) CTO, LiteLLM


[Moe Khalil](https://www.linkedin.com/in/moe-khalil-73a2371a1/) AI Product Engineer, LiteLLM


[Kerry Lu](https://github.com/kerry-berri) Member of Technical Staff, LiteLLM


[Tin Lo](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tinchi-lo/) AI Product Engineer, LiteLLM


Today we're launching **LiteLLM Customer Management** for AI-native companies using the gateway. If you're building an agent on LiteLLM and need to track spend and set budget limits for your customers by their organizations, teams, and individual members, this is for you.


## Who is this for?​


For AI-native companies building production agents using LiteLLM AI Gateway who need to run their agents profitably, with positive ROI.


## The problem​


With B2B AI agents, cost tracking gets complicated across customer organizations, teams, and individual members. If you sell pay-as-you-go credits or usage-based plans, actual spend can exceed what your customer paid and hurt your margin.

That's a bunch of glue code to build around your agent. Since LiteLLM is already your source of truth for model costs, we're exposing APIs to track customer spend, set budgets, and build these controls into your product.


## How to use LiteLLM AI Gateway for this problem​


Point your agent to LiteLLM AI Gateway and send your customer's organization alias and member ID:


- OpenAI Responses
- LangChain Deep Agents


```text
import   os        from   openai   import   OpenAI       client   =   OpenAI  (         api_key  =  os  .  environ  [  "LITELLM_API_KEY"  ]  ,         base_url  =  f"  {  os  .  environ  [  'LITELLM_BASE_URL'  ]  .  rstrip  (  '/'  )  }  /v1"  ,      )     raw_response   =   client  .  responses  .  with_raw_response  .  create  (         model  =  os  .  environ  [  "LITELLM_MODEL"  ]  ,           input  =  "Write a short welcome message."  ,         max_output_tokens  =  128  ,         extra_headers  =  {               "x-litellm-customer-org-alias"  :     "Acme"  ,               "x-litellm-customer-member-id"  :     "acme-alice"  ,           }  ,      )     response   =   raw_response  .  parse  (  )      print  (  response  .  output_text  )      print  (  "LiteLLM call ID:"  ,   raw_response  .  headers  .  get  (  "x-litellm-call-id"  )  )
```


Install with` pip install openai` .


```text
import   os        from   deepagents   import   create_deep_agent     from   langchain_openai   import   ChatOpenAI       model   =   ChatOpenAI  (         model  =  os  .  environ  [  "LITELLM_MODEL"  ]  ,         base_url  =  f"  {  os  .  environ  [  'LITELLM_BASE_URL'  ]  .  rstrip  (  '/'  )  }  /v1"  ,         api_key  =  os  .  environ  [  "LITELLM_API_KEY"  ]  ,         use_responses_api  =  True  ,         default_headers  =  {               "x-litellm-customer-org-alias"  :     "Acme"  ,               "x-litellm-customer-member-id"  :     "acme-alice"  ,           }  ,      )     agent   =   create_deep_agent  (  model  =  model  )     result   =   agent  .  invoke  (  {  "messages"  :     [  {  "role"  :     "user"  ,     "content"  :     "Say hello to Alice."  }  ]  }  )      print  (  result  [  "messages"  ]  [  -  1  ]  .  text  )
```


Install with` pip install deepagents langchain-openai` . Configure the model for the authenticated customer; pass the same identity to any other models the agent calls.


That's it for attributing the call. LiteLLM resolves the member's customer team and organization and records the spend. The same headers work with Responses, Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages.


Use your application key and a gateway model alias.` LITELLM_BASE_URL` is the gateway root URL;[register the customer first](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/customer_management/track-customer-spend#2-import-a-customer) , and select their identity from your authenticated session.


Follow a request into spend logs to see its customer organization, team, member, and cost. Demo data.[View full size.](https://docs.litellm.ai/img/customer_portal/launch-spend-log-dark.webp)


### Set customer budgets that protect your margin​


If a member buys $100 in credits, set a $60 budget for actual spend to protect your margin. Set separate budgets for the customer organization, each team, and each member:

Illustrative overlapping views of the same member usage. Do not add organization, team, and member spend together.


The same request's cost rolls up from the member to their team and organization. Here, the member hits their $60 cap while both parents still have room, so further requests pause.


Choose the organization cap and default member profile when you onboard a customer. These examples use a 30-day budget period:


- API
- LiteLLM UI


```text
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \      "$LITELLM_BASE_URL/management/v1/customer_organizations" \      --header "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_ADMIN_KEY" \      --header "Content-Type: application/json" \      --data '{        "customer_org_id": "org-acme",        "alias": "Acme",        "budget": {          "max_budget": 1000,          "budget_duration": "30d"        },        "default_budgets": [{          "name": "default-user",          "max_budget": 60,          "soft_budget": 48,          "budget_duration": "30d"        }],        "default_budget_template": "default-user"      }'
```


Use a server-side proxy admin credential as` LITELLM_ADMIN_KEY` .[Add the customer's teams and members](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/customer_management/track-customer-spend#2-import-a-customer) ; new members inherit the default profile.


Open **Customer Management → Customers → your customer → Settings** . Use **Set budget** or **Edit budget** to set **Spend limit (USD)** and **Reset period** . Select a member's **Budget template** for its default allowance.


Customer member spend and budget windows in the latest LiteLLM UI. Seeded demo data.[View full size.](https://docs.litellm.ai/img/customer_portal/launch-member-caps-dark.webp)


At the cap, LiteLLM rejects new requests based on recorded spend. Leave room for accounting delays and requests already in flight.


### Give default users and power users different profiles​


Some customers need more allowance. Create a power-user profile, then assign its returned` budget_id` when you create new members. Use the same APIs in your product so your customer's admins can manage these profiles.


```text
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \      "$LITELLM_BASE_URL/management/v1/customer_organizations/org-acme/default_budgets" \      --header "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_ADMIN_KEY" \      --header "Content-Type: application/json" \      --data '{        "name": "power-user",        "max_budget": 90,        "soft_budget": 72,        "budget_duration": "30d"      }'
```

When a member reaches their $60 cap, use the budget webhook to alert your team or open an approval request. Your receiver formats the notification from LiteLLM's JSON event.[Configure and test delivery](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/customer_management/track-customer-spend#1-set-up-budget-webhooks) ; reconcile missed alerts with usage reads because delivery is best effort.


### Approve a temporary increase when your customer upgrades​


When the customer buys another $50 in credits, their total becomes $150. After approval, apply a temporary $90 cap on actual spend, as shown above.


Set` INCREASE_EXPIRES_AT` to a future timestamp with a timezone, then apply the temporary member override:


```text
curl --fail-with-body --request PATCH \      "$LITELLM_BASE_URL/management/v1/customer_members/acme-alice" \      --header "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_ADMIN_KEY" \      --header "Content-Type: application/json" \      --data "{        \"budget_override\": {\"max_budget\": 90},        \"budget_override_expires_at\": \"$INCREASE_EXPIRES_AT\"      }"
```


Your product manages credit purchases and balances. LiteLLM applies the spend allowance until it expires; the organization and team caps still apply. Use the[approval APIs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/customer_management/api_reference#budget-increase-requests) if your workflow needs a review queue.


### Put the usage and budget controls in your own product​


Put usage next to the customer's credits and top-up options. Our APIs let your backend fetch actual spend and budget settings, so the customer sees the same costs you use for chargebacks:


Demo usage across three models, with 13 days of activity. Track the customer's total and inspect the model costs behind it.[View full size.](https://docs.litellm.ai/img/customer_portal/launch-usage-overview-dark.webp)


Fetch complete organization totals for a date range:


```text
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error --get \      "$LITELLM_BASE_URL/management/v1/customer_organizations/daily/activity/aggregated" \      --header "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_ADMIN_KEY" \      --data-urlencode "customer_org_ids=org-acme" \      --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-11-01" \      --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-11-30"
```


Read` metadata.total_spend` ,` total_tokens` , and` total_api_requests` . Fetch caps from the organization, team, and member records; keep admin credentials on your backend and authorize each customer's access. Your billing system applies your prices and collects payment.


### Keep serving requests with a lower-cost model​


Give a customer's dedicated virtual key an Opus allowance, then configure a lower-cost fallback for when that model allowance runs out. The customer can keep using your agent while they still have room in their overall budget.

Illustrative recorded spend and purchased credit value, before other expenses. Per-model key allowances trigger the switch; customer hard caps still apply.


Set` model_max_budget` and` budget_fallbacks` on the key with your configured model aliases. These[per-model key budgets](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/users#-virtual-key-model-specific) require Enterprise. A shared key pools its model budget across callers; customer organization, team, and member hard caps still stop requests when exhausted. See[Budget Fallbacks](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/budget_fallbacks) for the API setup.
